elements.label: Full-frame film-leader flash: clapperboard shot cuts through film-strip / colour-chart frames to a white flash
elements.change_other: film-leader flash frames (1-2 frame insert of film sprockets and colour-chart, then overexposed white)

sfx_review.label: unsure
sfx_review.note: Short narrow-band low-frequency thump at the cut to white, right after the broadband slate-clap burst (~0.8-0.92 s). Shape is not a rising reverse swoosh; could be a projector/impact thump, but too ambiguous to label.

pattern.description: After a live-action clapperboard slate, the edit inserts a couple of film-leader frames (sprocket holes, colour-chart swatches) and then flashes to an overexposed white frame, as a celluloid-style transition into the keynote.
pattern.why_premium: Analog film-burn vocabulary (slate, sprockets, colour chart, white flash) signals a crafted, cinematic production and gives the opening a tactile, behind-the-scenes texture instead of a generic logo sting.

build_hint.gsap: Hard-cut sequence on the HyperFrames timeline: tl.set(slate, {autoAlpha: 0}).set(leaderFrames, {autoAlpha: 1}).set(leaderFrames, {autoAlpha: 0}, '+=0.042').set(whiteFlash, {autoAlpha: 1}); optionally gsap.fromTo(leaderFrames, {x: 0}, {x: -60, duration: 0.08, ease: 'none'}) for the sprocket slip; no easing on cuts (step).
build_hint.remotion: Use <Sequence> blocks of 1-2 frames each (slate -> leader still -> white AbsoluteFill); optional interpolate(frame, [0, 2], [0, -60]) translateX on the leader frame. No spring; step changes only.

notes: Only one candidate box (b01, full frame). The camera verdict pan_left reflects the film-strip slipping across the leader frames, not a real camera move on the scene. The slate clap itself (broadband burst before x001) is not a candidate.
